faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.q1: How do I get access to the iOS beta?
faq.a1: Tap "Download on TestFlight" and you'll be redirected to Apple's TestFlight app. The whole process takes under 2 minutes.
faq.a2: Yes. Beta access is completely free, and beta riders keep full access at no cost when we launch publicly.
faq.a3: Zyflow works with any e-bike. You set your battery capacity and riding style, and we adapt route planning to your setup.
faq.a4: Android is in development. Join the waitlist and we'll email you as soon as a beta spot opens.
faq.a5: Use the in-app feedback option or contact us at support@zyflow.eu — we read every message.
faq.b1: Zyflow is a route planning app built for e-bike riders. It plans cycling routes with automatic charging stop suggestions, factoring in your battery range, elevation, wind, and temperature so you can ride further with confidence.
faq.page.q2: What bike types does Zyflow support?
faq.b2: Zyflow supports e-bikes, road bikes, gravel bikes, touring bikes, and mountain bikes. When setting up your profile, you select your bike type and enter your e-bike's range on a full charge. Zyflow uses this to calculate battery estimates along your route.
faq.b3: Zyflow is free to download and use.
faq.page.q4: Which platforms is Zyflow available on?
faq.b4: Zyflow is available on iOS and will be available also on Android.
faq.page.q5: How does Zyflow calculate my route?
faq.b5: Zyflow sends your start point, destination, and any waypoints to a cycling router. The result is a cycling-optimized route that accounts for roads, paths, and elevation.
faq.page.q6: How does Zyflow estimate my battery along the route?
faq.b6: Battery estimation uses your entered e-bike range combined with real physics: elevation gain, headwind or tailwind, temperature, and your rider weight. Weather data is fetched live so the estimate reflects actual conditions on the day of your ride. For rides longer than three hours, Zyflow also considers the weather forecast at your estimated arrival time.
faq.page.q7: How does Zyflow decide where to place charging stops?
faq.b7: Zyflow finds charging stations within a corridor along your route (5 km either side by default), clusters nearby options, and picks the best stop using a scoring system that penalizes large detours. If a stop requires rebuilding the route geometry, Zyflow re-routes through the charger and stitches the segments back together. You can also add or remove charging stops manually.
faq.page.q8: Can I adjust how far off-route Zyflow looks for chargers?
faq.b8: Yes. The corridor width is set by your maximum detour preference in your bike settings. The default is 5 km either side of your route.
faq.page.q9: Can I add my own stops or waypoints?
faq.b9: Yes. You can add charging stops manually during planning. GPX route import is also supported if you want to follow a pre-planned path.
faq.page.q10: Where does Zyflow get its charger data?
faq.b10: Charger data comes from our partners and is stored in Zyflow's own database. Information includes operator, network, available sockets, fees, access type, and opening hours where available.
faq.page.q11: Does Zyflow show real-time charger availability?
faq.b11: No. Zyflow does not currently show live occupancy or real-time status. We recommend verifying availability directly with the charger operator before relying on a specific stop.
faq.page.q12: Can I filter chargers by connector type or charging speed?
faq.b12: Not during route planning. Connector type and power details are shown on each charger's detail screen when available. You can also report connector information when submitting a missing charger.
faq.page.q13: Can I report a missing charger?
faq.b13: Yes. Use the "Add a charger" option in the app to submit a missing charging station, including connector type and other details.
faq.b14: No. An active internet connection is required for route planning, battery estimation, and loading charger and POI data. The app will show a warning if you lose connectivity.
faq.b15: Not currently. Zyflow is a route planner and visualizer. You plan your route in the app and follow it on the map, but there is no turn-by-turn guidance.
faq.page.q16: Can I import or export GPX files?
faq.b16: Yes, both are supported. You can import a GPX file to follow an existing route, and export any planned route as a GPX file to use in other apps. Zyflow can also open GPX files shared directly from other apps on your device.
faq.page.q17: Do I need an account to use Zyflow?
faq.b17: Yes. An account is required to use the app. Sign-up takes just a moment and supports Apple Sign-In on iOS.
faq.page.q18: What is saved to my account?
faq.b18: Your saved routes and saved places are stored in your account and synced across devices. Your name is also stored in your profile. Bike preferences (range, weight, detour settings) are currently stored locally on your device only.
faq.b19: Account deletion is not yet available directly in the app. To request deletion of your account and data, please contact us at support@zyflow.eu. We will process the request within 30 days.
faq.page.q20: My battery estimate seems off. Why?
faq.b20: Make sure your e-bike range is set correctly in your bike preferences. The estimate is based on your entered range adjusted for the actual elevation, wind, and temperature of your route. Very aggressive riding or extremely cold conditions can push real-world consumption beyond the estimate.
faq.page.q21: Zyflow is not finding chargers along my route.
faq.b21: Try widening your maximum detour distance in bike settings. If chargers are genuinely missing in your area, you can submit them directly in the app using the "Add a charger" option.
faq.page.q22: The route looks wrong or takes an unexpected path.
faq.b22: Check that your bike type is set correctly, as this affects which roads and paths the router considers. If the issue persists, please get in touch and share the route details so we can investigate.
faq.page.q23: The app is not working and I have no internet connection.
faq.b23: Zyflow requires an internet connection for route planning and live data. Check your connection and try again.

about.page.title: About the app
about.page.why.title: Why Zyflow exists
about.page.why.body: Real e-bike riding is messy. Headwinds, steep climbs, charging stations that are out of service. Zyflow plans around all of it so you can focus on the ride.
about.page.feature1: Plans your route around your actual range, not just distance.
about.page.feature2: Accounts for climbs and descents so your battery estimate is accurate.
about.page.feature3: Checks conditions at each segment, not just at your start point.
about.page.feature4: Finds chargers along your route and factors stop time into your plan.
